clue.text: Doctor cuts up curtains for the alternative therapists

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic slashes the curtains, apparently on behalf of practitioners of fringe medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal working on CUTS UP and CURTAINS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Practitioners who insert needles at set points on the body are a familiar kind of complementary-medicine therapist.

clue.text: Frank swallows drug covered in sugar

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the drug goes into the word for frank

parts.note: frank means candid, open and honest
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An outspoken person takes a pill that has a sugary coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or peel preserved with a sugar crust is described as candied.

clue.text: Safe after national event

indicators.note: safe comes after national, so the word for national goes in front

parts.note: a Pole is a national of Poland
a vault is a strongroom or safe

explanation.surface: A strongbox is placed after some country's big occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping over a high bar with a long flexible pole is an athletics field event.

clue.text: Dark times for hero during hearing

indicators.note: during a hearing things are taken in by ear, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: knights are the heroes of chivalric romance

explanation.surface: A gloomy period for a champion while a court case goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' pretends to be a legal hearing; it signals that KNIGHTS, said aloud, gives the answer's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between sunset and sunrise are the periods meant by dark times.

clue.text: Leather displayed at parade

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are set out afresh, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leather goods are shown off at a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A tapadera is the leather hood on a Western saddle's stirrup, an unfamiliar word built entirely from AT and PARADE.
explanation.definitionFit: This leather cover fitted to the front of a stirrup protects a rider's foot, so leather stands for the item.

clue.text: Game artist left in the country

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter who abandoned a sport now lives in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rural belongs to farmland and villages rather than towns, which is what in the country describes.

clue.text: Respect new staff

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the previous word are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Show proper regard for the fresh employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; here it is a rod, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ornamental rod carried as a symbol of authority is a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Essex has no borders in this direction

definitions.text: Essex has no borders in this direction

parts.words: Essex has no borders in this direction
parts.note: strip the first and last letters from the county name and the three letters left are the compass abbreviation of a bearing, written out in full

explanation.surface: A remark that an English county is open on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSEX without its first and last letters leaves SSE, the abbreviation for the bearing. Essex is a county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearing halfway between due south and south-east is the compass point described.

clue.text: Having horror story penned?

parts.note: read 'horror story' as a writer's work, but the real sense is a horror of being shut in a pen

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone has written a scary tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests written; the cryptic sense is penned in, enclosed, and the horror is a fear of confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a dread of confined spaces is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Pine stage positioned in the field

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A pine tree is set up as a stage out in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, LONG LEG is a fielding position near the boundary behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a place where a cricket fielder stands, so it is a position out in the field.

clue.text: Upstart backs popular music at meeting-place, mostly

indicators.note: backs here means turns round, so the music word is read in reverse

parts.note: rap is a form of popular music

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a venue is a meeting-place

explanation.surface: A social climber supports pop music at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like supports; it reverses RAP to PAR. VENUE loses its last letter to give VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer who has risen suddenly in wealth or status without acceptance is an upstart.

clue.text: Gatecrasher is college boy holding horrible French wine

indicators.note: holding means containing, so college and boy enclose the mixed-up wine

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
Ted is a boy's name

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of the wine word are rearranged

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A party crasher turns out to be a student holding nasty plonk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' scrambles VIN to NVI, which sits between UNI and TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives at a party without being asked is a gatecrasher; the adjective describes such a guest.

clue.text: Something to secure top of lectern at church

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A device to fix the top of a reading stand in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple bar fastening for a door or gate is something used to secure it.

clue.text: Hymn featuring new duet with me

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A hymn including a fresh piece for two singers with me in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'new' works on DUET and ME together.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin song of praise to God is a well-known canticle sung in church services.

clue.text: Experts on each old Shakespearian character

parts.note: pros are experts
per means each, as in 'a pound per head'

explanation.surface: Specialists comment on every old figure from the Bard's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The exiled magician duke of The Tempest is one of the Bard's best-known characters.

clue.text: Just like Jack to crack safe and find a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it open, so the letters of safe are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A thief named Jack breaks open a safe and finds a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack Tar) is an old name for a sailor, so 'Just like Jack' means sailor-like. 'Crack' rearranges SAFE to SEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jack Tar spends life at sea, so being like one means being given to ocean voyaging.

clue.text: Privileged English schoolboy goes round school — such language!

indicators.note: goes round means one piece surrounds another, so the schoolboy encloses the school letter

parts.note: an Etonian attends Eton, the exclusive English public school

explanation.surface: A posh pupil swears all around the school: what language!
explanation.walkthrough: 'such language!' looks like disapproval of swearing; it defines a Baltic tongue. ETON is an elite boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Finnic tongue spoken in the Baltic republic beside Latvia is the kind of language meant.

clue.text: Expect too much of voter when making silly request

indicators.note: silly suggests the word is jumbled into a nonsensical order

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: An elector is too demanding when making a daft demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden someone with more work than they can manage is to demand too much of them.

clue.text: English box upon the grass

parts.note: to spar is to box
upon here has the sense of to, as in 'press upon' and 'press to'

explanation.surface: An English boxer fights on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is the verb to fight, SPAR, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough Mediterranean plant used for making paper and rope is a kind of grass.

clue.text: Religious leader takes time to chat

indicators.note: takes means the leader adds the next piece after himself

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader

explanation.surface: A clergyman makes time for a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chatting at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to rabbit is to talk on and on, so it means chatter.

clue.text: Some soldiers cross a bridge

indicators.note: cross is read as angry or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit crosses a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like the verb to go over, but it is the anagram signal for A BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A military formation of several battalions is a body of soldiers.

clue.text: This prize upset artist

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: This trophy annoyed the painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like annoyed; it reverses DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition of an achievement, like a prize.

clue.text: Wished to dance with journalist

parts.note: to hop is to dance, as at a hop
ED, an editor, is a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Longed to dance with a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped is to have wanted something to happen, the same as wished.

clue.text: For example small drop with a lot of ice

definitions.text: For example small drop with a lot of ice

parts.words: For example small drop with a lot of ice
parts.note: a small drop of spirit topped with plenty of ice is one instance of what is poured at a bar

explanation.surface: An illustration: a tiny tot served on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay suggests D plus RINK (a lot of ice), but nothing in the clue plainly gives D, so it reads as a cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirit served over ice is one kind of beverage.

clue.text: Worker producing desired effect

definitions.meaning: an employee, especially a factory hand or a secret agent
effective, in force, as a rule that is in operation

explanation.surface: An employee who gets results.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a skilled hand or agent, and the adjective means functioning or effective.

clue.text: Italian artist takes fresh brie outside new inn

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other, so the cheese letters wrap the inn letters
fresh suggests remaking, so the letters of the cheese are rearranged
new indicates a fresh order for the letters of inn

explanation.surface: An Italian painter takes newly made brie outside a new inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns BRIE into BERI, and 'new' turns INN into NIN, which sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the great Baroque sculptor and architect of Rome.

clue.text: Beastly types return plate with hint of supper on

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the next piece after the first
return means turn back, so the plate word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Brutes send back a dish with a whiff of dinner on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses LAMINA to ANIMAL; 'hint of' gives S from supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures such as beasts are a kind of being, so beastly types are these creatures.

clue.text: Hide with Dirk — it's to do with spying

parts.note: to cloak is to hide
and means together with
a dirk is a short dagger

explanation.surface: Concealment with a man named Dirk: it's all about espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirk' looks like a man's name, but it is the Scottish dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the secretive, melodramatic world of espionage and intrigue.
